She knows that for communities to thrive, every person in the United States must have easy access to high-quality, affordable health care that centers patients, not special interests.    Image Dexter founded the Democratic Doctors Caucus to bring medical expertise to the policymaking table. Through this caucus, she is working to ensure that health policy decisions are rooted in scientific evidence, compassion, and good, efficient governance that prioritizes healthy communities through incentivizing the system to achieve outcomes that lead to good public health.   Congresswoman Dexter is a strong defender of Medicaid, which provides lifesaving care to children, low-income families, people with disabilities, and older Americans. She is pushing back against efforts to cut or restrict access to this essential program and is committed to strengthening the nation’s safety net.   As a doctor and a legislator, Congresswoman Dexter recognizes that health does not exist in a vacuum. She is leading efforts to push the federal government to acknowledge and address the public health impacts of climate change, including worsening air and water quality, respiratory illness, and extreme weather events. Climate | Representative Maxine Dexter Skip to main content   Climate The climate crisis is an existential threat. Oregonians know all too well how climate-fueled disasters—from deadly wildfires to extreme freezes—can wreak havoc on our communities. As a lung and critical care doctor, Congresswoman Maxine Dexter has seen firsthand how climate change and poor air quality impact our health and well-being. The connection is undeniable: heart disease, stroke, respiratory illness, and cancer rank among the top causes of death, and particulate air pollution dramatically worsens them all. These impacts fall hardest on Black, Brown, Indigenous, and economically-disadvantaged communities.   Image Dexter knows the federal government must take bold, immediate action. Addressing the climate crisis is an opportunity to improve public health, advance environmental justice, and create a more equitable economy for all Oregonians.   House Natural Resources Committee   Image Dexter serves on the House Natural Resources Committee, with jurisdiction over forests, public lands, national parks, oceans, energy and mineral resources, and the federal relationship with Native American Tribes throughout the United States.   Elected as Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, Dexter is responsible for overseeing federal agencies within the Natural Resources jurisdiction. In this capacity, she is fighting to protect Oregon’s natural resources from Trump’s polluter-first agenda.     More on Climate Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. Takes on Big Oil with Three-Bill Package to Protect Taxpayers September 3, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON , D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) introduced a three-bill package to hold Big Oil accountable and stop these companies from passing their costs onto American taxpayers. Democracy | Representative Maxine Dexter Skip to main content   Democracy Congresswoman Maxine Dexter is committed to protecting our democratic institutions, defending the Constitution, and ensuring that every American has equal access to the ballot box. In this moment of crisis, with basic rights under assault, Congresswoman Dexter knows that the defense of democracy is not optional—it is an obligation.   Voting Rights   Image Congresswoman Dexter understands that the right to vote is the cornerstone of our democracy and has taken several strides to protect it. She forced a vote in the House to expose the SAVE Act, legislation that would disenfranchise millions of married women, seniors, and those a part of marginalized communities.    She helped reintroduce the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, over 60 years after John Lewis and hundreds of civil rights heroes put their lives on the line in Selma, Alabama. This bill acknowledges their bravery and modernizes the Voting Rights Act of 1965, paving a way forward to ensure every voter, regardless of background or race, has access to the ballot box.    Image Congresswoman Dexter also joined a Congressional Voting Rights Caucus letter denouncing the constitutionality of Trump’s voting executive order, and she signed a House Resolution reaffirming that the 22nd Amendment bars Trump from seeking a third term.   Due Process and Constitutional Protections   Congresswoman Dexter is using every tool available to defend due process and the rule of law. After Maryland resident Kilmar Abrego Garcia was wrongfully deported and sent to a notorious prison in El Salvador without legal recourse, Congresswoman Dexter traveled there to demand his release and meet with U.S. Embassy officials and local human rights advocates. As a critical care physician, she’s trained to act in moments of crisis—and she continues to do so in defense of our constitutional rights.   She is sounding the alarm on a broader constitutional crisis: the Trump administration is detaining children, arresting judges, and denying immigrants and legal residents their right to due process. Veterans | Representative Maxine Dexter Skip to main content   Veterans Congresswoman Maxine Dexter serves on the House Veterans' Affairs Committee, including the Subcommittees on Health and Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs. In these roles, she advocates for policies that ensure veterans receive the health care and benefits they have earned and deserve.   Image Dexter is deeply committed to ensuring that Oregon veterans receive the care and support they have earned, advocating for policies that uphold their dignity and well-being On January 23, 2026 Dexter became the first first-term House Democrat to pass a bill into law. Her legislation, the Focused Assistance and Skills Training for Veterans’ Employment and Transition Success (FAST VETS) Act, makes crucial improvements to the Department of Veterans Affairs’ Veterans Readiness and Employment (VR&E) program to give veterans the best benefits possible. Dexter has led efforts to protect veterans' access to reproductive health care. She co-authored a letter with over 130 House Democrats urging the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to maintain its policy allowing abortion services in cases of rape, incest, or when the life of the veteran is at risk, opposing attempts to rescind this access.   In response to the Trump administration's federal hiring freeze, which affected over 40,000 positions at the VA, Dexter joined fellow committee members in demanding transparency and action to prevent disruptions in veterans' access to health care and benefits.   Dexter is committed to ensuring that Oregon veterans receive the care and support they have earned, advocating for policies that uphold their dignity and well-being.   More on Veterans House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Unanimously Passes Rep. Immigration | Representative Maxine Dexter Skip to main content   Immigration Congresswoman Maxine Dexter is committed to protecting our neighbors from unlawful and inhumane immigration policies. Dexter supports defunding and dismantling ICE. She believes our immigration system must be centered on humanity, due process, and dignity—not chaos and cruelty.   Since taking office, Dexter has helped secure the release of 14 Oregonians who were wrongfully detained by immigration agents. That includes leading the effort in 2025 to free Oregon mother and small business owner Jackie Merlos , who was detained with her four U.S. citizen children at the U.S.-Canadian border and held for weeks without access to legal counsel. In 2026, Dexter traveled to Dilley, Texas, to advocate for the release of the Crespo-Gonzalez family from the nation’s largest child and family detention facility. The family was detained after taking their sick second grader to an urgent care clinic in Portland, despite having an active asylum case. Dexter successfully escorted the family out of detention and back home to Oregon.    In Congress, Dexter was one of the first lawmakers to support articles of impeachment against Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem for her unlawful and inhumane mass deportation agenda. Additionally, Dexter has introduced legislation to bring accountability and transparency to immigration enforcement, including the CLEAR ID Act, which requires ICE agents to identify themselves, and the Restoring Access to Detainees Act, which ensures detained individuals can contact loved ones and speak with legal counsel.   More on Immigration Dexter, Randall Send Letter Demanding Answers Over Inhumane Condition at ICE Detention Center August 31, 2026 Press Release Members call attention to reports of inedible food, lack of medical care and alleged sexual assault occurring inside the facility Issues : Congress Democracy Immigration Dexter, Randall Make Unannounced Oversight Visit to Northwest Detention Center After Reports of Hunger Strike and Unsafe Conditions August 15, 2026 Press Release TACOMA, Wash.  – Today, U.S. Reps. Max

LGBTQIA+ Equality | Representative Maxine Dexter Skip to main content   LGBTQIA+ Equality Congresswoman Maxine Dexter knows that everyone—no matter who they are or who they love—deserves a life of dignity, safety, and full equality under the law. As a strong advocate for the LGBTQIA+ community, she is committed to advancing policies that protect civil rights and ensure equal treatment in every aspect of life.   Dexter helped introduce the Equality Act, landmark legislation that would explicitly prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing, education, public accommodations, and more. She believes no one should be denied basic rights for being their most authentic selves.    Image She is also fighting to ensure LGBTQIA+ service members and veterans receive the care and respect they have earned and deserve. Dexter supports efforts to eliminate discriminatory policies in the military, expand access to gender affirming health care at the VA, and ensure that all veterans are treated with fairness and dignity.   Equality is foundational and Congresswoman Dexter will continue working to build a country where LGBTQIA+ individuals are protected, valued, and free to thrive.   Issues Climate Democracy Economic Opportunity Health Housing Immigration LGBTQIA+ Equality Reproductive Rights Veterans
